info.name: UNBLOCK-AI API
info.description: Endpoints exposed by the Express server (src/app.ts, src/routes/). Generated to match docs/api/api-documentation.md. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner in folder order: Health, Auth, Drafts, Workflows, Selection, Tasks, Approvals, Error cases. Most requests need a bearer token - the collection-level auth reads it from {{adminToken}}, captured by the 'Login (admin)' request in the Auth folder, so running Auth first is what makes everything after it authenticate automatically. The Approvals folder needs a token copied by hand out of the console mailer's stdout log after 'Start task (dispatch approval chain)' -- it cannot be fully automated by the Collection Runner.

item.name: Drafts
item.description: Create a draft, then extract a workflow from it. draftId is captured from 'Create draft' and used by the rest of this folder.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "IT Faculty Overseas Leave",
  "text": "Any undergraduate student of the Faculty of Information Technology who intends
to travel overseas during the academic term must obtain prior approval before
leaving the country.

The student submits a request stating their full name, index number, the
destination country, the departure date, the return date, and the reason for
the trip.

The request first goes to the student's Academic Advisor for approval. Once the
Academic Advisor approves, it goes to the Head of the Department of Information
Technology. At any point an approver may either approve the request, reject it
with a reason, or ask the student for more information, in which case the
student is asked for the missing detail and the request returns to that same
approver.

If the total duration of the trip exceeds 30 days, the request must additionally
be endorsed by the Dean of the Faculty after the Head of Department has
approved.

When all required approvals are complete, the student is issued a signed
overseas leave authorization letter and notified that it is ready for
collection."
}

request.description: Idempotent by SHA-256 of text. Text taken from src/data/samples/demo-drafts/it_overseas_leave.txt.

body.raw:
{
  "text": "Departmental Event & Workshop Organization

When a department submits a request to organize an event or workshop, the submission is split into three sub-requests that are handled independently: hall booking, guest speaker security clearance, and refreshments budget approval.

Hall booking is reviewed by Campus Administration (the hall warden). They confirm the venue name and the confirmed venue capacity, or reject the booking.

Guest speaker security clearance is reviewed by the Security Office, independently and concurrently with the hall booking — neither waits on the other.

Refreshments budget approval is automatically placed on hold when the event request is submitted, because the catering cost estimate depends on the confirmed venue capacity. As soon as the hall booking is approved, the refreshments approval is released and sent to the Finance Office, using the confirmed venue capacity to size the catering budget.

The event is considered fully organized only once all three sub-requests — hall booking, security clearance, and refreshments approval — are approved. A single consolidated status page shows the state of all three. When everything is approved, the requester is notified by email that the event is confirmed."
}

request.description: Returns the next pending required requirement, then pending optional ones, then { requirement: null, complete: true }. Run this + 'Submit next requirement value' in a loop (Collection Runner) until complete is true. The test script stores the requirement's key AND type into {{requirementKey}} / {{requirementType}}, so the next request can build a value the validator will accept.

value is polymorphic — its shape depends on the requirement's type, and the API coerces strictly (src/utils/task/value-validator.util.ts):

| type | accepted value |
| --- | --- |
| string / text / phone / enum / file | any string |
| email | a string matching user@host.tld — e.g. requester_email |
| number | a finite number (numeric strings are coerced) |
| boolean | true / false, not "true" |
| date / datetime | "YYYY-MM-DD" |
| person | { "name": ..., "email": ... } — the actor:* requirements |

The pre-request script reads {{requirementType}} (set by 'Get next requirement') and builds a matching sample into {{requirementValue}}, so a Collection Runner loop of next -> values fills every requirement — including the email-typed requester_email — without hand-editing the body. Override {{requirementValue}} manually (as raw JSON) to send a specific value.

Requires status: ready (run Finalize task first). Dispatches the entry step(s), issues each an approval token, and emails the assignee. With MAIL_TRANSPORT=console (default) the email is logged to the server's stdout — copy the token out of that log line into {{approvalToken}} to drive the Approvals folder.
Requester-facing view distinct from 'Get task by id' — status, current_steps, timeline, and (once rejected) who rejected it and why.

Downloads the completion-document PDF record — a re-render of every value the requester supplied plus the approval trail, regenerated on each call rather than stored. Only available once the task status is completed; run this after the approval loop below has driven the task to completed: true, or expect a 409.

item.name: Approvals
item.description: Token-authenticated, not session-authenticated. Copy the token out of the console mailer's stdout log (from 'Start task (dispatch approval chain)' in the Tasks folder) into {{approvalToken}} before running these. Re-run 'Start task' -> copy token -> Get approver view -> Submit decision for each subsequent step until the task completes or rejects.

request.description: 404 if the token is malformed or unrecognized (deliberately not 401 — does not confirm or deny a token's existence). A re-fetched, already-decided token still returns 200 with already_decided: true rather than erroring.

Edit the body to { "outcome": "rejected", "reason": "..." } or { "outcome": "request_more_info", "reason": "..." } to exercise the other branches — a reason is required whenever the step's outcome config sets include_reason: true. A used token 409s on replay.

exec: pm.test("response has outcome and status", function () { pm.expect(json).to.have.property("outcome"); pm.expect(json).to.have.property("status"); });
